title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Several Provisions on Establishing an Execution Interview Mechanism
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the Several Provisions on Establishing an Interview Mechanism for Enforcement Work

Fa Fa [2016] No. 7

To: All Higher People's Courts of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the Higher People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

The Several Provisions on Establishing an Interview Mechanism for Enforcement Work are hereby issued. Please carefully comply with and implement them.

March 8, 2016

Several Provisions on Establishing an Interview Mechanism for Enforcement Work

To further standardize the enforcement work of courts across the country, to timely discover and correct problems such as passive enforcement and illegal enforcement in the performance of enforcement duties by lower-level courts, and to promote the resolution of "difficulty in enforcement," these Provisions are formulated in accordance with the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and other laws and judicial interpretations, and in light of the actual circumstances of court enforcement work.

Article 1 For the purposes of these Provisions, "interview" refers to a supervision measure in enforcement work whereby the Supreme People's Court, when circumstances specified in these Provisions occur, meets with responsible persons of a Higher People's Court who have failed to perform or have inadequately performed their duties, to give admonitory talks, point out problems, and order rectification and correction.

Article 2 An interview may be conducted under any of the following circumstances:

(1) Where, through the national court enforcement case process information management system, it is found that within the jurisdiction of a Higher People's Court, overdue enforcement cases exceed 5% of the accepted cases, or there are other serious passive enforcement problems such as no justified reason for prolonged inaction on cases with property available for enforcement;

(2) Where, through channels such as petitions, it is found that illegal enforcement and other issues are prominent within the jurisdiction, causing adverse effects;

(3) Where, with respect to supervisory or supervised cases for which the Supreme People's Court has issued clear opinions, those opinions are not implemented within the prescribed or reasonable time limit without justified reason, or are not implemented properly;

(4) Where key enforcement tasks or special work deployed by the Supreme People's Court are not implemented or the implementation fails to meet the required standards;

(5) Other circumstances warranting an interview.

Article 3 Where the Enforcement Bureau of the Supreme People's Court, in the course of performing its enforcement supervision and management duties, deems that a circumstance specified in Article 2 exists and that an interview is necessary, it may, after approval by the bureau's executive meeting, first issue a "Preliminary Notice of Interview" to the Higher People's Court to be interviewed, pointing out the existing problems, setting forth rectification requirements and a time limit, and specifying that failure to implement rectification will result in a formal interview.

After receiving the "Preliminary Notice of Interview," if the Higher People's Court fails to implement the rectification requirements without a reasonable explanation, the Supreme People's Court, upon approval by the relevant leading official of the court, shall formally issue a "Notice of Interview" to the Higher People's Court and initiate the interview procedure.

Article 4 The "Notice of Interview" shall generally be issued by the Enforcement Bureau of the Supreme People's Court seven working days before the interview, informing the interviewee of the subject, method, time, place, and participants of the interview.

Article 5 The interview work shall be organized and implemented by the Enforcement Bureau of the Supreme People's Court. When necessary, a leading official of the court may be requested to participate.

An interview may be conducted solely by the Enforcement Bureau of the Supreme People's Court, or may be conducted jointly with other departments such as the Supervision Department of the Supreme People's Court. If other departments are invited to participate jointly, communication and consultation on the interview matters shall be carried out in advance.

Article 6 The specific procedure for an interview is as follows:

(1) Explain to the interviewee the subject and purpose of the interview;

(2) Present the handling opinions to the interviewee, specifying the rectification requirements and time limit;

(3) The interviewee expresses their position on implementing the handling opinions and rectification requirements.

Article 7 After the interview, a record of the interview shall be prepared, which shall include the subject of the interview, handling opinions, rectification requirements and time limit, and other main contents.

The interview record shall, after being reported to and approved by the leading official who authorized the interview, be issued under the name of the Enforcement Bureau of the Supreme People's Court to the interviewee.

Article 8 The Enforcement Bureau of the Supreme People's Court shall supervise and guide the interviewee in implementing the handling opinions and rectification requirements proposed in the interview, and shall report the implementation status level by level to the leading official who authorized the interview.

If the handling opinions and rectification requirements are implemented on time, no further action shall be taken. If they are not implemented within the time limit or are not implemented properly, the following measures may be taken:

(1) Report to the Party leadership group of the Higher People's Court to which the interviewee belongs;

(2) Circulate a notice within the national court system;

(3) If there is suspicion of illegal or disciplinary conduct, report the circumstances to the Supervision Department of the Supreme People's Court and propose that an investigation and handling of the responsible persons be conducted;

(4) Deduct appropriate points in the assessment of targets for comprehensive social management in public security.

Article 9 For interviews conducted on matters of public concern, the circumstances and results of the interview may be disclosed to the public as appropriate, and media representatives and members of the public may be invited to observe the interview.

Article 10 These Provisions shall take effect on March 9, 2016.
